Join us underground for a day of spooky season fun for all ages. 
Free Halloween programming will take place at the museum entrance and in the Blast Tunnel. Stop by for activities for youth and families, a spooky photo backdrop, and trick-or-treating (while supplies last). No admission or booking is required to take part in the free programming.  
We invite you to continue your Halloween visit inside the Diefenbunker with general admission — explore the museum and take part in a Halloween-themed scavenger hunt along the way.  
Date
Saturday, October 31  
Time
Halloween programming: 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.
Museum admission and scavenger hunt: 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.  
Cost
Halloween programming: Free
Museum admission and scavenger hunt: Purchase a general admission or guided tour ticket to enter the museum. Tickets can be purchased in advance or on site.  
Costumes are welcome all day for visitors of all ages.  
>>PLAN YOUR VISIT
   

Please note that the multiple levels, stairs, and narrow hallways in the Diefenbunker can make the museum difficult to navigate with a stroller, and there is no elevator available for public use. While an accessible stair lift is available, we recommend bringing a baby carrier instead of a stroller, if this is a feasible option for you. Learn more about accessibility.

The OAG’s Learning and Engagement team offers Art Talk phone calls in partnership with The Good Companions Seniors’ Centre and other seniors’ organizations. 
Experience a taste of the local world of art by joining us for engaging discussions about the OAG’s diverse exhibitions and collections, where our expert guide provides in-depth descriptions of artworks and the meaning behind them. Simply dial 1-844-237-9847 to join the conversation and be encouraged to share personal experiences and memories evoked by the artwork! 
THIS PROGRAM IS FREE 
All you need is a regular telephone to participate! 
Phone calls take place on the last Tuesday of each month, at 10:45 am. 
Art Talk phone calls are also featured in the Seniors’ Centre Without Walls program, which coordinates a calendar full of voluntary phone-in opportunities that enrich the lives of local seniors. Mail-outs of Art Talk images are provided to those who register in advance. 
Seniors who are interested in taking part in upcoming Art Talk conversations, and opportunities alike, can do so by reaching out through this link:
The Good Companions Centre

column2: Operation Whisky: A Festive Fallout Fundraiser
column3:
Join us on Saturday, November 21, 2026 for the return of our signature annual fundraiser, with a retro festive twist! 
Travel back in time to the 1950s and escape the looming nuclear winter as you stay warm underground in a decommissioned fallout shelter, delighting in a mid-century holiday party with whisky tastings, themed cocktails, tasty treats, a silent auction, and other festivities. 
Enjoy unique flavours and a slice of the past, while contributing to the preservation of Canada’s Cold War story. 
Tickets
Individual: $160.00 


Four whisky tastings
A selection of food pairings and appetizers
Access to full cash bar
Tax receipt for a portion of the ticket price


Designated Driver: $100.00 


A selection of food plates and appetizers
Two non-alcoholic beverages
Access to non-alcoholic beverages at the cash bar
Tax receipt for a portion of the ticket price


Sponsor a Full Table: $1,500 


Tickets for 8 people
Four whisky tastings per person
A selection of food pairings and appetizers
Access to full cash bar
Bonus gift for each attendee
Recognition as a sponsor in event promotions and signage
To sponsor a table, please contact marketing@diefenbunker.ca.

Tickets must be purchased in advance. 

>> RESERVE YOUR TICKETS

Event details

6:00 p.m. Doors open. Join the party and check out the cash bar, appetizers, silent auction, and festive activities throughout the lower levels of the museum.
6:30 p.m. Event kick-off and introductions.
6:45 p.m. Sommelier introduces the whisky selections. Whisky and food pairings available at stations throughout the evening.
9:00 p.m. Silent auction closes.
9:30 p.m. Event ends.

Silent auction
We look forward to featuring incredible prizes from local businesses in the event’s silent auction. To inquire about donating items to our silent auction, please contact marketing@diefenbunker.ca.

By sponsoring this event, you can put your organization at the forefront of important community engagement and impact. Learn more about the available sponsorship opportunities (opens in new tab) and contact marketing@diefenbunker.ca for more information. 
What cause am I supporting?
A portion of your ticket for this fundraising event is a donation to the Diefenbunker: Canada’s Cold War Museum. Ticket purchasers will be issued a tax receipt after the event for this donation. 
The Diefenbunker is an impressive four-storey underground facility that operated as the country’s central communications headquarters during the Cold War, ready at any moment in case of a nuclear attack. Today, it is a one-of-a-kind museum, national historic site, and independent charitable organization. 
Your support through our fundraiser will contribute to our preservation and conservation efforts, along with our ability to offer high-quality exhibitions and educational programs to visitors year-round. Thank you for preserving an important window into the past, as we continue to share important history lessons and strive to build a more peaceful future.

The Diefenbunker was an active military base for 32 years throughout the Cold War. We invite you to learn why we remember as you explore Cold War stories at the Diefenbunker.
This Veterans’ Week (November 5–11), the Diefenbunker honours those who have served and those who continue to serve, including Indigenous veterans on November 8. 
Through special programming, we reflect on the impact of conflict and work towards a more peaceful future. 
November 5 to 8 and 10 to 11

Visit the Bank of Canada Vault for a space of reflection and remembrance.
Discover stories of Indigenous veterans through our exhibition An Inuit Story: The DEW Line(opens in new tab).
Watch oral history videos(opens in new tab) of Cold War veterans, on display outside the Machine Room.
Hear museum volunteers share their stories and personal experiences from serving during the Cold War.

November 10


In addition to our extended experience guided tours, two special tours will be available. Spots are limited and tickets must be reserved in advance. Reserve your tickets.(opens in new tab)

Curatorial Tour, 12:30 – 2:30 p.m.
Discover secret history of the Diefenbunker — what came before it, and once-classified plans for its operations in the event of a nuclear attack on Canada. You will explore historical context surrounding the Cold War that led to the construction of the Central Emergency Government Headquarters (the Diefenbunker) and will learn about Canada’s preparations for a nuclear war that were never realized, including the plans for after a bomb hit and the implications on citizens across the country. 
Collections Tour, 12:30 – 2:00 p.m.
Discover the Diefenbunker as Canada’s most significant Cold War artifact. You will explore the bunker’s unique architectural features that were designed for surviving a nuclear attack and will learn about how we preserve the facility today for the continued enjoyment of museum visitors. 
November 11

Enjoy free general admission to the museum. Reserve your tickets.(opens in new tab) Guided tours will not be offered.
A moment of silence will be observed at 11 a.m. throughout the museum. After this time, we invite you to lay your poppy on our wreath in the Bank of Canada Vault. The wreath will be brought to the West Carleton War Memorial at the end of the day.

The museum will be closed on November 9. 

Interested in supporting our Veterans’ Week initiatives? Sponsorship opportunities are available. (opens in new tab)

You’re invited to the Creative Opportunities Conference, a free event taking place at the Ottawa Art Gallery’s Alma Duncan Salon on Sunday, November, 8, 2026. 
This one-day event is a fantastic opportunity to learn about a range of arts education, creative careers, and artistic development opportunities available right here in the greater Ottawa-Gatineau region. The COC is designed to connect the region’s community of arts professionals, recent graduates, and adult learners with local arts/visual media, and community organizations that offer programs and experiences designed to enrich your artistic practice, professional skills, and personal development.
